name: Mercury capsule
dispatch: The Mercury capsule was designed to be the smallest thing that could keep a person alive in space — and it shows. There was no room to do much but sit; the astronaut wore the spacecraft as much as rode it. But its shape solved the era's hardest unsolved problem — how to come back. The blunt end, coated in a shield built to char and carry the heat away, turned reentry from a fatal certainty into something survivable, and its cone was the first American answer to the question of what a crewed spacecraft even looks like. Every capsule since — Gemini, Apollo, Dragon — is a descendant of this cramped little cone.
description: The cone-shaped capsule that carried six American astronauts on Project Mercury between 1961 and 1963. Tiny enough that John Glenn famously described being "spam in a can" — but it proved orbital flight was achievable for the United States.
